title: PMKLC: Parallel Multi-Knowledge Learning-based Lossless Compression for Large-Scale Genomics Database

problem.claim: Large-scale genomic databases require effective lossless compression for backup, storage, transmission, and management.

gap.claim: Existing learning-based lossless compressors are limited by inadequate compression ratio, low compression and decompression throughput, and poor compression robustness.

contributions.claim: PMKLC uses an automated multi-knowledge learning-based compression framework to improve compression ratio and robustness.
PMKLC combines a GPU-accelerated (s,k)-mer encoder with data block partitioning and Step-wise Model Passing for throughput and parallel acceleration.
PMKLC provides PMKLC-S for resource-constrained single-GPU execution and PMKLC-M for multi-GPU acceleration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present PMKLC as a novel Parallel Multi-Knowledge Learning-based Compressor.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors benchmark PMKLC-S/M against 14 baselines across 15 real-world datasets covering different species and data sizes.
Compared with baselines, PMKLC-S/M achieve average compression-ratio improvements of up to 73.609% and 73.480%, and average throughput improvements of up to 3.036X and 10.710X, respectively.
The authors report best robustness, competitive memory cost, and greater stability under probability-distribution perturbations, including operation on memory-constrained devices.

narrative_sequence.summary: Learning-based lossless compression supports large-scale genomic database operations.
Existing approaches face compression-ratio, throughput, and robustness limitations.
PMKLC addresses these limitations through multi-knowledge learning, GPU encoding, parallel mechanisms, and two execution modes.
The authors evaluate PMKLC-S/M against traditional and learning-based baselines on 15 real-world datasets.
The authors report improvements in compression ratio and throughput, along with strong robustness and competitive memory cost.

source_observation.claim: The system separates resource-constrained single-GPU operation from multi-GPU acceleration through two compression modes.

interpretation.claim: Providing deployment modes aligned with hardware constraints can broaden a system's applicability.

application.claim: When designing resource-intensive data systems, offer configurations that match distinct compute and memory environments.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which application scenarios benefit most from each mode.

source_observation.claim: The reported evaluation varies species and data sizes and compares against both traditional and learning-based baselines.

interpretation.claim: Evaluating across heterogeneous datasets and baseline families can expose performance variation across data conditions.

application.claim: For data-compression evaluations, include varied data distributions, scales, and relevant competing method families.

exception.claim: The abstract does not provide per-dataset results or details of the evaluation protocol.
